items.title: At England's Sutton Hoo, archaeologists uncovered ghost-like outline of Anglo-Saxon body in sand
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Recent excavations at Sutton Hoo have revealed a unique 'sand body' along with various grave goods. Archaeologists discovered this rare feature, which indicates prior burials in the area. The findings suggest insights into the burial practices of Anglo-Saxon communities. Tools and ornaments found with the sand body provide context for understanding the individual's life. These discoveries challenge the focus solely on royal burials in the Sutton Hoo region.

items.title: Punjab teacher plants 10,000 trees over 18 years, keeps mission alive
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: For 18 years, Ranjit Singh Chinna has passionately championed environmental activism in Punjab, inspired by the lack of shade along a road in his community. He has successfully planted approximately 10,000 trees in public spaces and along highways, demonstrating his commitment. Alongside this, he participates in various community services, including removing carcasses and cleaning public areas, showcasing the profound impact that one dedicated individual can have on their environment.

items.title: IBM tells visa holders in its biggest division: Leave the US or leave IBM by Dec 31
items.author: TOI TECH DESK
items.description: IBM is ending US visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in IBM Consulting, its biggest division with over 150,000 employees. Affected H-1B workers can relocate to IBM roles outside the US, mostly in India, or leave the company by December 31, 2026. The move comes amid the US administration's crackdown on H-1B visas and foreign tech hiring, including a one-time $100,000 filing fee.
